name: Sodium beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB salts)

lead: BHB salts are supplements that bind the ketone beta-hydroxybutyrate to minerals such as sodium, potassium, magnesium or calcium. People on low-carb diets use them hoping raised ketones ease appetite and energy dips and help them get leaner.

BHB is the main ketone body the liver makes during fasting and low-carb eating, and the salts supply it directly, raising blood BHB without fasting. Research is limited to small physiology studies, and fat loss from the salts has not been tested in published trials found here. Most products are racemic, so only about half is the form the body uses.

paras: They are mixed as a powder drink or taken as capsules, usually alongside a ketogenic or low-carb diet or around fasting. Users take them for appetite and energy during the adaptation period.
The salts add a mineral load such as sodium and slightly raise blood pH. Long-term safety data in healthy dieters are limited.

angle.text: BHB salts are used by people on low-carb diets who hope raised blood ketones ease appetite and shift energy toward a leaner body. They do raise blood BHB; effects on fat loss have not been tested.

lead: Sodium beta-hydroxybutyrate is a salt form of beta-hydroxybutyrate (BHB), the main ketone body the liver makes during fasting, prolonged exercise and low-carbohydrate diets. [1][2] In supplements, BHB is bound to sodium, potassium, magnesium or calcium; most products are racemic, so only about half is the biologically used D form. [1]
Sellers market ketone salts as a way to raise blood ketones without dietary restriction, with claims about appetite, energy and fat loss. [1] These claims are commonly discussed in fat-loss contexts.

Human studies of BHB administration are mostly small physiology trials in healthy people and in patients with diabetes or heart failure; none located in the sources reviewed tests BHB salts for fat loss or appearance.

paras: Ketone bodies are produced by the liver and used by tissues when glucose is scarce; the two main ones are acetoacetate and beta-hydroxybutyrate. [2] Classic studies showed that during prolonged starvation the brain uses ketone bodies in place of much of its glucose. [3][4] Reviews have discussed ketone bodies in ketogenic diets, insulin resistance and mitochondrial metabolism. [5]
Salts slightly raise blood pH, whereas esters lower it, according to Wikipedia. [1] The most-studied ester is a separate compound, described in its own entry.

Registered studies of exogenous ketosis include safety and tolerability of free BHB, effects on kidney function, cognition during exercise-heat stress, brain ketone metabolism in type 1 diabetes, a BHB ester in ALS, BHB in type 1 and type 2 diabetes, and nutritional ketosis in heart failure. [6][7][8][9][10][11][12] Several of these use esters or free BHB rather than salts. No studies found testing sodium BHB salts specifically for fat loss or appearance.
